title: Insulin pump: setup and changing the infusion set
what: A pump is a small device that delivers insulin under your skin in small amounts through a thin tube. You change the catheter in your skin yourself every few days.
why: For diabetes, when your doctor has decided to switch you from injections to a pump.
duration: changing a set usually takes 10 to 15 minutes; the first training at the clinic takes a few hours
tell_doctor: If your sugar is often too low or too high
If redness or hard lumps appear at the set sites
If you cannot see the pump screen well or find small parts hard to handle
If you plan a trip, sports or a pregnancy

prepare.title: Training
prepare.text: The first insertion and setup are usually done with a doctor or nurse. Only your doctor sets the doses.

prepare.title: Supplies
prepare.text: Keep a stock at home of sets, reservoirs, batteries and an insulin pen in case the pump breaks.

prepare.title: When to change
prepare.text: Change the set in the daytime, when you can check your sugar 2 to 3 hours later. Not before bed.

prepare.title: Cleanliness
prepare.text: Wash your hands and put the antiseptic and everything you need on a clean table.

bring: The pump and a new infusion set
steps: Wash your hands and check the expiry dates of the insulin and the set
Fill a new reservoir with insulin without air bubbles
Put the reservoir in the pump and fill the tubing as you were taught, until a drop shows at the end
Choose a new spot on your belly or another site, away from the last one
Wipe the skin with antiseptic and let it dry
Insert the catheter with the inserter and remove the guide needle
Fill the cannula from the pump menu, if your model needs it
Check your sugar after 2 to 3 hours
feel: A short prick when the catheter goes in
In the first days the pump on your body feels strange, then you barely notice it
after: Change the set usually every 2 to 3 days - the time is in the set's instructions
Write down set changes and sugar
Always carry sweets and a spare insulin pen
Show your pump data to your doctor regularly
red_flags: High sugar that does not come down after a correction - change the set and call your doctor
Nausea, vomiting, smell of acetone or severe thirst - see a doctor urgently, and if you get worse, call your local emergency number
Redness, pain or pus at the set site
The person is unconscious or having seizures - call your local emergency number

faq.q: Can I shower with the pump?
faq.a: Usually the pump is disconnected for a shower. Whether you can use it in water is in the instructions for your model.
Switch to injections with a pen, using the backup plan from your doctor. If you have no plan, call your doctor.

reminders.text: Pump set change today. Do it in the daytime and check your sugar after 2 to 3 hours.
